newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks down 1.2 pct, led by gold stocks.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks down 1.2 pct, led by gold stocks.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 93.185 +0.015 Gold NY 318.00 Lon fix 318.00
AUD open $0.7439 (Mon cl $0.7454) CRB Index 232.22 -3.35
*Plummeting gold shares triggers correctional decline on stock market after record run. Volume 205.42 million, value A$325.26 million, 1,051 stocks traded, 240 steady, 112 up, 699 down
The Australian stock market experienced its biggest intra-day fall since April 1 on Monday in the first major set-back to the 18 percent rally over the past three months.
"Gold is the catalyst for an overall correction after the hard run. I wouldn't be surprised if we get a correction over the next few weeks," one Sydney-based institutional dealer said.

At 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), the All Ordinaries index had lost 33.2 points to 2,679.8, while September share price index futures contracts were 41 points lower at 2,707, a 27.2 point premium to the underlying index.
Gold stocks continued its dramatic fall as the precious metal's price again fell sharply in offshore trade, hitting a 12-year low of U$313.19 before recovering to U$318 an ounce.
By midday, the sector index had lost another 8.1 percent and has now dived around 18 percent since the Reserve Bank on Thursday said it had sold two-thirds of gold reserves.
"This is panic selling going on at the moment. People are jumping out in droves and things are being driven down so hard," said Hartley Poynton broker Justin Hondris.
Normandy Mining, the heaviest in the sector, came down to its lowest levels in four and a half years.

The stock fell eight cents to A$1.24, while Plutonic Resources dived 57 cents to A$3.31. Other major gold stocks to slide included Newcrest Mining which fell 27 cents to A$2.75 and Lihir Gold which lost 14 cents to A$1.80.
Acacia Resources dipped 18 cents to A$1.27, its lowest level since listing.
Although gold shares were clearly in everybody's focus, few blue chips escaped the negative trend.
"All the blue chips have had a wonderful run and so they will all be part of a correction" one dealer said.
Bellwether Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd fell 27 cents and broke through the 19 dollar barrier to trade at A$18.98. WMC lost 35 cents to A$7.78 while Rio Tinto fell 30 cents to A$22.15.
National Australia Bank lost nine cents to trade at A$19.31, while ANZ dipped 10 cents to A$9.73.
Declines outnumbered advances by more than six to one, while about one fifth of traded shares were stable.
Media shares were stronger. News Corp gained two cents to A$6.53 while Publishing and Broadcasting shrank three cents to A$7.89.

In other local markets, Australian bonds were held to a tight range with sentiment underpinned by the strength of U.S. Treasuries, but with the market reluctant to push higher ahead of Thursday's job data. By 12.25 p.m. (0225 GMT), 10-year T-bonds were two basis points lower at 6.82 percent.

The Australian dollar tried desperately to put some distance between it and an 18-month low at the midsession, but with scant success as it traded at US$0.7439 compared to US$0.7454 on Monday afternoon.
Most blue chips suffer correctional declines.
Media sector among the strongest.
-- Martina Barsoum, Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-180
